title: Lemire's half-degree conjecture holds for the infinite family n = 2*3^k
statement: For every integer k >= 0, the polynomial f_k(x) = x^(2*3^k) + x^(3^k) + 1 over F_2 is the cyclotomic polynomial Phi_(3^(k+1)), is irreducible over F_2 of degree n = 2*3^k, and satisfies deg(f_k - x^n) = 3^k = floor(n/2). Hence for every n in {2, 6, 18, 54, 162, 486, 1458, ...} there is an irreducible polynomial of degree n over F_2 whose nonleading terms have degree at most floor(n/2); Kaser--Lemire holds at these degrees.

formal.statement: ; NOT a single SMT instance: the statement is a universally quantified family over k. Each instance (fixed k) is a decidable irreducibility check over F_2, machine-verified by flint for k = 0..6 (n up to 1458); the family is proved by the cyclotomic argument, not by SMT.

evidence.detail: Phi_(p^m)(x) = Phi_p(x^(p^(m-1))) gives Phi_(3^(k+1)) = x^(2*3^k)+x^(3^k)+1 (Lidl-Niederreiter, Finite Fields, Thm 2.47). Phi_m mod p is irreducible over F_p iff p is a primitive root mod m; 2 is a primitive root mod 3^(k+1) for all k>=0 (ord_3(2)=2, 2 primitive mod 9, lifting theorem). deg(f_k - x^n) = 3^k = floor(n/2).

flint 0.9.0: f_k irreducible over F_2 and ord_(3^(k+1))(2) = 2*3^k for k = 0..6 (n = 2,6,18,54,162,486,1458); and x^(2k)+x^k+1 is F_2-irreducible for 1<=k<=81 exactly when k in {1,3,9,27,81} (powers of 3). Reproduced independently in the lemire-signed-trace lane.

provenance.established_by: lane lemire-signed-trace (input-type-2 construction search); classical cyclotomic irreducibility (Lidl-Niederreiter; Fredricksen-Wisniewski 1981; Golomb-Lee)

prior_art.citation: H. Fredricksen and R. Wisniewski, On trinomials x^n+x^{n/2}+1 and x^{8l+-3}+x^k+1 irreducible over GF(2), Information and Control 50 (1981)
prior_art.establishes: x^{2k}+x^k+1 is irreducible over GF(2) iff k is a power of 3

prior_art.citation: R. Lidl and H. Niederreiter, Finite Fields, Thm 2.47
prior_art.establishes: Phi_m mod p irreducible iff p is a primitive root mod m; the prime-power cyclotomic identity

notes: The m = 2 special case of F:gf2-lemire-monomial-composition-family: x^2+x+1 has order 3, and Theorem A with t = 3^k gives Phi_(3^(k+1)) = x^(2*3^k)+x^(3^k)+1. It retains an independent proof (cyclotomic irreducibility does not go through Lidl-Niederreiter Thm 3.35), which is why it is kept as a separate fact rather than folded in. It was the first infinite family recorded in THIS ledger, but not in the literature: Emil Jerabek gave exactly this family in a comment on the MathOverflow question that originated the conjecture (lemire, 'Can we always find such an irreducible polynomial of degree n where degree(p(x)-x^n) <= n/2?', 23 Nov 2011; Lahtonen notes it is an exercise in Lidl-Niederreiter). The irreducibility is classical cyclotomic theory. Scope of THIS family: density zero (n = 2*3^k) and even n only. It is the unique CYCLOTOMIC window family (for Phi_(p^a) the second term sits at degree (p-2)p^(a-1) <= phi/2 iff p <= 3, and p = 2 is reducible, forcing p = 3) -- but the first version of note 08 also claimed it was the unique PROVABLE family and that no provable family reaches odd n, and both of those are FALSE: the seed x^3+x+1 of order 7 gives the odd family n = 3*7^k by the same theorem. Not blocked by the moduli barrier (note 03) or the symmetry barrier (note 06) because it reads the class description and exhibits a witness (input type 2 of note 05). The all-n statement still needs the phase-aware estimate F:gf2-lemire-cylinder-twist-sup-bound.
